newsitem.title: USA: Green Mtn Power net up on higher revenues.
newsitem.headline: Green Mtn Power net up on higher revenues.

text.p: Green Mountain Power Corp Friday reported third quarter earnings were $0.67 per share of common stock, up from $0.60 per share, a year earlier as operating revenues increased 11.7 percent.
The revenue rise was primarily due to a 5.25 percent retail rate increase that went into effect in June 1996 and a 3.8 percent increase in electricity sales to commercial and industrial customers.

"The retail rate increase that took effect this summer was intended to cover anticipated higher costs for power purchased from independent power producers, Hydro-Quebec and the Vermont Yankee nuclear generating plant," chief financial officer Christopher Dutton said.

Power supply expenses increased 12.2 percent in the third quarter of 1996 over the same period in 1995 primarily due to higher costs for power purchased from Hydro-Quebec, to costs associated with the scheduled refueling outage at Vermont Yankee, and an increase in mandated purchases of electricity from independent power producers, he said.

Dutton reported that the Vermont Yankee plant, in addition, has accelerated certain maintenance and operating projects to provide added assurance of compliance with license and regulatory requirements.

Depreciation and amortization expenses increased 8.6 percent in the third quarter of 1996 over the same period in 1995 primarily due to the amortization of expenditures related to energy conservation programs and to additional investment in the company's electric distribution facilities, it said.
